fact: Kenya's ICT Cabinet Secretary unveiled Kabogo.AI on 27 August 2026, an AI assistant being developed to route citizens to the right government agency, service or resource, which Kenyans.co.ke reports is still being prepared and will launch once review safeguards are in place.

The Kenya Revenue Authority says it has unveiled a WhatsApp tax filing service powered by an AI chatbot, Shuru, through which taxpayers access pre-filled details, file returns, generate invoices and obtain compliance certificates.

Kenyans.co.ke reports, from Digital Health Agency tender documents seen on 25 August 2026, that the agency floated seven tenders including an AI-driven RMNCAH digital health platform, an AI-managed national blood bank system and an AI birth-and-death notification registry for Taifa Care.
GIZ says Kenya is currently developing a GovStack-based AI-powered chatbot on the eCitizen platform to answer citizens' questions.

GovStack says a conversational AI chatbot is being designed for Kenya's eCitizen platform, with the Kenya Film Commission as pilot institution and service design just started, under the EU-co-financed IDGC programme.
The Business Registration Service page says GIZ support developed an AI-powered chatbot that provides information on business registration services; it does not say the chatbot is in service.

Kenya's Ministry of Information, Communications and the Digital Economy, with Konza Technopolis and UNDP, launched an AI Accelerator Programme inviting developers to submit AI applications to improve public services, applications closing September 2026.
